title: The Rabbit Lands Encyclopedia
note: IN DEVELOPMENT! Every page here is either original Rabbit Lands reference text or is built from the client's own catalogues, so a recipe, spell or book that changes in the data changes here too. Report corrections through the Rabbit Lands project issue tracker.

skillNotes.attack: How hard you hit and how often you connect. The server rolls it; the client only shows what it said happened.
skillNotes.defense: How often a blow misses you, and how much of one your armour is allowed to soak.
skillNotes.harvesting: How quickly you take from a resource node, and which nodes the server will let you start on at all.
skillNotes.alchemy: Essences, bars, and the ingredients the rest of the trades are built out of.
skillNotes.magic: The ceiling on which spells you may cast, and on the power you may ask for.
skillNotes.potion: Everything that ends up in a vial, from the plain healing draught upwards.
skillNotes.summoning: Calling a creature to fight beside you, and the stones and flesh it costs.
skillNotes.manufacturing: Metal work: armour, weapons, and the plates and rings they are made from.
skillNotes.crafting: Rings, medallions and the small worked goods that need a mould.
skillNotes.engineering: Devices and traps, and the tools that build them.
skillNotes.tailoring: Thread, cloth, dye, and every garment made from them.
skillNotes.ranging: Shooting at distance. The server refuses a shot at a target standing too close.
skillNotes.overall: Not a trade of its own. It is the sum the server keeps across all the others.

categories.title: The World
categories.summary: Nymara, its hours and its weather
categories.intro: Eloria is played on Nymara. The server owns the world and the clock; this client draws what it is told and asks for the rest.

entries.title: What the server decides
entries.summary: Why nothing here is a guess
entries.body:
Every fact in this client came from the server: where you stand, what you carry, what you hit and what hit you. The client picks the artwork and the camera, and nothing else.

That is worth knowing when a click seems to do nothing. Asking to walk somewhere, to attack someone, or to take from a node is a request. The server answers it, and the answer may be no. What you see on screen is the answer, not the request.

entries.title: Day and night
entries.summary: Six real hours to a Nymaran day
entries.body:
A full day is 360 game minutes and one game minute is one real minute, so the world turns through dawn, noon, dusk and night over six hours.

The light you see follows the same curve the server uses to decide how far creatures can be seen, so a dark night is dark for both of you.
facts: The clock face on the lower HUD

entries.title: Marks and waypoints
entries.summary: The server's marks and your own
entries.body:
A waypoint is the server's: it appears on your map and reports the distance as you move.

A mark is your own. It never leaves this client, and it is drawn in a different colour so you can tell your own note from something the world told you.

entries.title: Weather and light
entries.summary: Rain, cloud, and the sky over each map
entries.body:
Weather belongs to the map you are standing on. The server states it, the client renders it, and it changes the light rather than only the picture.

An interior does not take the sky's weather. Walking indoors changes what lights you and what you can hear, which is why a doorway can feel like a different time of day.

categories.title: Combat
categories.intro: Combat is entirely the server's. This client asks it to start a fight and then reports what came back.

entries.title: Attacking
entries.summary: Three ways to start a fight
entries.body:
There are three ways to ask for a fight, and all three send the same request.

Hold Alt and click a living creature or player. The move icon on the lower HUD turns into the attack icon while Alt is held, so you can see what a click will do before you make it; let Alt go and it turns back.

Or click the attack icon on the HUD. That latches: the icon stays lit and every click attacks until you choose the move icon again, and holding or releasing Alt does not undo it.

Or select a target and press the attack key.

Whatever you choose, the server walks you into reach, decides whether the fight may start, and refuses the ones that may not.
facts: stays on until you pick the move icon

entries.title: Ranging
entries.summary: Bows, arrows and distance
entries.body:
A bow and matching ammunition let you attack from a distance. The server refuses a shot at a target standing too close - move away and try again.

Each shot is announced twice: once as an aim, once as the arrow leaving. The damage is resolved by the server and arrives separately.

entries.title: Armour and damage
entries.summary: What a suit is allowed to soak
entries.body:
Armour is worn in pieces - helm, torso, legs, boots and a shield - and each piece carries its own absorption and its own penalties. A heavy suit soaks more, and costs you accuracy and movement to wear.

What a piece absorbs is what the server allows it to take off a blow, not what it will take off every blow. The roll is still the server's.

entries.title: How perks work
entries.summary: Pick points, tiers, exclusions and gear
entries.body:
A perk is bought with pick points, and most of them are bought more than once. There are 32 perks on the shelf and 32 of them come in tiers.

Pick points come from overall levels: two for each, spent on attributes, nexus or perks, and never spent twice. Every tier of a perk costs 3 pick points, so owning one outright is 9; what climbs from tier to tier is the gold.

Some perks cannot be held together - Lucky Hitter and Lucky Dodger answer the same question from opposite sides, and so do Mirror and Life Stealing. The page for each perk says what it clashes with.

Worn gear can carry a perk. A cape does not simply grant one: it adds a tier, which means it is worth the same to a player who has bought all three as to one who has bought none - and it is the only way to reach the tiers above the third.

A removal stone takes back one tier and returns what that tier cost. At its highest tier a perk that says so can be switched off with the #perk command, which hands back the effect and not the pick points.

#list_perks names everything you hold, the tier you are at, and what that tier does.

categories.title: Harvesting
categories.summary: Taking things out of the ground
categories.intro: Everything the trades below are made from starts here.

entries.title: Harvesting
entries.summary: Nodes, levels, and why you stopped
entries.body:
Resource nodes belong to the server, not to the scenery. It tells the client which objects on the map can be gathered, what each one yields and what level it needs, so a node you can see is a node the server knows about.

Click a node to start. The server reports that harvesting has begun and reports again when it stops - because you moved, because your backpack filled, or because something interrupted you. The client never decides that you have stopped.
facts: clicking a node the server has described
moving, a full backpack, or the server

entries.title: Bags on the ground
entries.summary: What is dropped, and who may take it
entries.body:
Anything dropped becomes a bag standing on the ground where it fell. Opening one asks the server to describe it; what comes back is its contents at that moment and nothing older.

A bag is not yours. Another player standing over it sees the same bag and can take from it, and the server settles who got what.

entries.title: Storage
entries.summary: What a storage keeper holds for you
entries.body:
Storage is held by the server, one set of shelves per character, reachable from a storage keeper. Deposits and withdrawals are its decision; the window shows the shelves as they were when it last described them.

Carrying capacity applies on the way out. A withdrawal that would overload you is refused, and the goods stay where they were.

categories.title: Trade
categories.summary: Dealing with players and with the exchange
categories.intro: Two ways to move goods between people, both settled by the server.

entries.title: Trading and the exchange
entries.summary: Direct trades and the Nymara Exchange
entries.body:
A direct trade is between two players, and both must accept before anything moves. The server owns every step; the window shows what it has confirmed.

The Nymara Exchange takes listings and holds both goods and proceeds in escrow until they are collected.

entries.title: What a thing is worth
entries.summary: There is no fixed price list
entries.body:
Nothing in this encyclopedia states a price. The client is not told one, and a made-up figure would be worse than none.

What the pages below do state is what a thing costs to make: its materials, the level it wants, and the food it burns. That is the floor under any price, and it comes from the server's own recipe table.

categories.title: Alchemy
categories.intro: Alchemy turns what is harvested into the essences and bars the other trades consume.

categories.title: Manufacturing
categories.intro: Metal work. Armour is made in pieces - helm, torso, legs, boots and shield - and the same bars go into the weapons that beat them.

categories.title: Crafting
categories.intro: Crafting wants a mould more often than it wants a fire.

categories.title: Engineering
categories.intro: Things that are built rather than forged.

categories.title: Potions
categories.intro: A potion is mixed once and drunk once. What it does is the server's to apply.

categories.title: Tailoring
categories.intro: The longest recipe list in the client, and the one that most often wants a book first.

categories.title: Summoning
categories.summary: Calling a creature to your side
categories.intro: A summoning is paid for in stones and flesh, and the creature that arrives is the server's, not yours.

categories.title: Magic
categories.summary: Sigils, spells and the effects they leave
categories.intro: Choose a spell family, targeting mode and Power 1–10. Higher power replaces separate greater spells.

entries.title: Casting and power
entries.summary: One effect, ten power levels
entries.body: Own every listed sigil, carry the reagents and choose a power your Magic level and nexus support. Higher power increases healing, damage, protection or duration and costs more ether and reagents. Heal and Poison have no separate Greater versions. The spell window can be searched and filtered by targeting mode.

entries.title: Self, Target, Allies and Burst
entries.summary: Choose who receives a spell
entries.body: A base name such as Heal affects you. Target selects one actor within 15 tiles; Bolt also means one target. Allies affects you and party or guild members within four tiles. Burst selects a location within 15 tiles and affects eligible actors within four tiles of it. Hostile spells respect party, guild and PK restrictions. Escape cancels target selection without spending resources.

entries.title: Damage, wards and Dispel
entries.summary: Match protection to the damage type
entries.body: Magic Bolt deals magic damage; Fire Bolt heat; Frost Bolt cold; Radiation Bolt radiation. Each has a Burst form and a matching ward. Elemental Ward combines heat, cold and radiation protection. Shield improves physical protection. Dispel removes poison, cripple, resistance reductions and drained stats. Magic Immunity temporarily blocks hostile spells.

entries.title: Transmute
entries.summary: Selected inventory items become gold
entries.body: Choose an inventory item and quantity. Review the required power and exact gold return before casting. Common items need Power 1, Uncommon 3, Rare 5, Epic 7 and Legendary 9. Their gold multipliers are 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 times the item base transmutation value. Only the selected quantity is consumed. Gold Coins and quest items cannot be transmuted.

entries.title: Recall and portal destinations
entries.summary: Higher power opens destination selection
entries.body: Recall at Power 1–4 returns you to Four Gates. At Power 5–10 choose a map with a portal entrance and the entrance where you will arrive. Maps with several entrances list each location. Blink remains a short teleport to a walkable place within 15 tiles.

categories.title: Books
categories.summary: What must be read before it can be made
categories.intro: A book is read once. Until the server records that you have read it, the recipes it teaches are refused however high your level is.

categories.title: Maps
categories.intro: Each region is its own map on the server. Crossing between them is a change of map, not a walk across a seam.
